chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Ma'qil al-Qarmaysani narrated to us, from Ibn Taher, who said: I was standing behind my father, and with him were Abu al-Salt al-Harawi, Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal. My father said: 'Let each of you narrate a hadith to me.' Abu al-Salt al-Harawi said: 'Ali ibn Musa al-Rida narrated to me, and God was pleased with him as his name indicates, from his father Musa ibn Ja'far, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali, peace be upon them all, who said: The Messenger of God, peace be upon him and his family, said: Faith is speech and action.'
When we left, Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal said: 'What kind of chain of narration is this?' My father said to him: 'It is the snuff of the insane; if the madman snuffs it, he recovers.'

key_terms.سَعُوطُ الْمَجَانِينِ: Snuff for the insane (metaphor for a simple but effective cure)

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of faith according to Ali al-Rida in this hadith from Al-Khisal?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the Shia doctrine that faith (Iman) comprises both verbal affirmation and practical deeds, a definition affirmed by Ali al-Rida. Shaykh al-Saduq’s father, al-Hasan ibn al-Fadl, uses the metaphor of 'saeet al-majanin' (a medicinal snuff that cures madness) to humorously validate the chain's authenticity against Ahmad ibn Hanbal’s scrutiny, suggesting that what may seem simple or 'mad' to critics is actually a potent, curing truth. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the unity of belief and action, distinguishing it from views that might separate them.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-68 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn Ma’qel al-Qarmaysani said, “I was standing with my father. Abu Salt al-Haravy, Ishaq ibn Rahoyeh and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal were also present there. My father said, “Each of you should narrate a tradition for me.” Abu Salt al-Haravy said, “Ali ibn Musa al-Ridha (MGB), who I swear by God was really pleasant as his name indicates, quoted on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far al-Kadhim (MGB), on the authority of his father Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of Ali ibn al-Hussein (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali (MGB), on the authority of his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said, “Faith consists of talking and action.”

When we left Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Hanbal said, “What form of chain of traditions was that?” My father said, “It is the healing medication for the insane. If they treat a mad man using it, he will be healed.”
